summary: The study investigates the atomic layer epitaxy (ALE) of InP and GaAs using in situ X-ray photoemission spectroscopy (XPS). The process involves the selective adsorption of Me(CH3)n precursors (Me = In or Ga, n = 1, 2, or 3) on the surfaces of InP and GaAs, which then decompose into atomic Me species. This self-limiting adsorption mechanism is crucial for the growth of high-quality semiconductor layers.
evidence: In situ observations of InP and GaAs grown by atomic layer epitaxy have been made, using an X-ray photoemission spectroscopy system combined with a metalorganic vapor phase epitaxial growth chamber, where In(CH3)3, PH3, Ga(CH3)3 and AsH3 were the source gases. It has been proved that Me(CH3)n precursors (where Me = In or Ga and n = 1, 2 or 3) decompose into Me atoms after being adsorbed on the InP and GaAs surfaces.
